declared_not_measured.cu_term: not carried: `fee_lamports` is the charged tx fee (network + priority); no per-CU price is recorded in this tape, so the (tip + CU) split of the M5 leg cost is declared, not measured, and is NOT used to shrink the p50/p90/p99 ladder.

justification: The p90/p99 fixed cost shipped as INLINE LITERALS in cost_authority.decompose (45_000 / 1_005_000) beside a properly named p50. Measured here from 91,735 of our own fills (fee_lamports = the tx fee the chain charged, network + priority): p50 10,000 (equal to FIXED_LAMPORTS_PER_LEG_P50, so the named constant and the measurement agree), p90 45,000, p99 1,005,000, mean 66,521 with max 400,005,000. The mean sits ABOVE the p90 because the distribution has a long priority-fee tail, which is exactly why a quantile ladder is the honest input and a mean is not: training stays at p50 (the measured typical leg), adversarial/gate scenarios take the conservative end (p90, and p99 for the worst-case fee spike). The compute-unit term is declared, not measured: fee_lamports carries no per-CU price, so the (tip + CU) split is not used to shrink this ladder.
